Q1: Formaldehyde exhibits significant known hazards across most categories, including carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive hazards (CMR1), environmental hazards (ENV1), and acute hazards via inhalation (IHL1), oral exposure (ORL1), and skin/eye contact (SKN1), as well as organ/systemic toxicity (OGN1). It also shows evidence of endocrine disruption (EDC2) based on an expanded scientific perspective beyond standard GHS classifications.
Q2: Formaldehyde is prominently featured on numerous lists of concern, notably as a Group 1 carcinogen by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) and on California's Proposition 65 list for its potential to cause cancer and reproductive harm. It is also identified as a potential endocrine disruptor by The Endocrine Disruption Exchange (TEDX) and is regulated under several key environmental and public health acts, including the Clean Water Act, Safe Drinking Water Act, and as a Hazardous Air Pollutant.
Q3: Formaldehyde is exceptionally well-characterized, evidenced by over 250,000 scientific literature references, which is vastly greater than the median for chemicals. Its precise molecular formula (CH2O) and classification as a 'Small Molecule' confirm its clear definition, alongside the complete absence of any data-deficient (Tier 4) hazard classifications.
